links.title: Bitcoin Core :: About
links.why: What the project says it is and who maintains it, which is the question behind this chapter's branch on the reference implementation.

links.title: Bitcoin Core :: Download
links.why: The binaries, the checksum file and the signature file; the page the verification exercise of this chapter starts from.

links.title: Bitcoin Core :: Releases
links.why: Every release with its notes, so a student can see what changed between the release this chapter checked and whatever is current when they read it.

links.title: Verify Binaries (contrib/verify-binaries)
links.why: The project's own script for checking a download against the signed checksums, and what its answers mean; the automated form of the hash-and-signature steps this chapter performs by hand.

links.title: UNIX BUILD NOTES (doc/build-unix.md)
links.why: The prerequisites and the build commands for a Unix machine, which is this chapter's build branch in the maintainers' own words.

links.title: Setup and running notes (doc/README.md)
links.why: What each shipped executable is for, and where the data directory and the configuration file live.

links.title: Implemented BIPs (doc/bips.md)
links.why: The list of improvement proposals the software actually implements, and from which version; the evidence behind any claim that Bitcoin Core supports a given standard.

links.title: Support for Output Descriptors in Bitcoin Core (doc/descriptors.md)
links.why: The descriptor language a modern wallet is written in, including the checksum this chapter recomputes.

links.title: RPC API Reference
links.why: Every remote-procedure call with its arguments and its result, to look up beside this chapter's interface branch.

links.title: Block Chain (Developer Reference)
links.why: The block header field by field, the compact target encoding and the Merkle tree; the reference for the figures this chapter recomputes from a real block.

links.title: Running A Full Node
links.why: What running a node costs in disk, bandwidth and time, and how to open the port; the practical side of this chapter's node-resources section.

links.title: Running Bitcoin - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: A long list of command-line and configuration options with short explanations, useful when deciding which ones a given machine needs.

links.title: Block hashing algorithm - Bitcoin Wiki
links.why: The header hash worked through with a real example, including the byte order that catches every beginner; the check on this chapter's own header computation.

links.title: PROV-O: The PROV Ontology
links.why: The vocabulary behind this chapter's linked-data section, where a verified download is described as data with a recorded origin.

_note: Every link was fetched over HTTPS on 2026-10-05 from this session and answered 200; the title recorded here is the title the fetched document itself carries (for an improvement proposal, the Title line of its own preamble), not a title written from memory. A proposal's status is quoted from its preamble too, because a student needs to know whether what they are reading is deployed, draft or superseded.
